name: Taurus Engineering And Manufacturing
old_description: Flexibility and rapid responsiveness is what makes Taurus Engineering a valuable partner for medical product developers.
about:
Taurus Engineering and Manufacturing operates from a 33,000-square-foot facility in St. Paul, Minnesota. The company traces its roots to 2008, when John Philipsen acquired Innovative Mold and rebranded it as Taurus Engineering. Since then, the privately owned business has focused on serving the medical device sector with injection molding and assembly services.

The firm specializes in precision injection molded components, complex subassemblies, and fully packaged assemblies for medical devices. Its capabilities include insert molding, over-molding with thermoplastic elastomers, and Class 7 cleanroom molding. The plant runs 20 injection molding machines ranging from 28 to 350 tons on a 24/5 schedule, and it maintains in-house toolmaking for single- and multi-cavity molds. Secondary operations, assembly, packaging, and supply chain management are offered under a complete contract manufacturing model.

Taurus serves medical product developers and OEMs, producing parts such as connectors, infusion sets, IV catheters, valve swivels, and heat-and-moisture exchangers. Customers range from early-stage startups needing rapid prototypes to established manufacturers requiring high-volume production and tool transfers.

The company emphasizes a "Thinking Outside the Box" philosophy, positioning itself as a strategic partner rather than a vendor. It highlights flexibility, rapid responsiveness, and a design-for-manufacturing approach to accelerate time to market and reduce costs. Its quality system is ISO 13485 certified by Intertek and FDA registered, supported by first-article inspections, IQ/OQ/PQ validations, PPAPs, and statistical process controls.
